timeline.text: Foundation: FastAPI backend, React + TypeScript frontend, PostgreSQL and a CI/CD pipeline.
Google, Azure and AWS OCR run in parallel on each section of the prescription; the most confident result wins.
Medical NLP: AWS Comprehend Medical extracts drugs and doses, Gemini corrects OCR errors and expands abbreviations.
253,973+ medicine records and RxNorm lookups added; confidence scoring routes uncertain results to review.
Upload, review and pharmacy screens connected end to end; prototype demoed.
Demo testing: 98–99% medicine names, 97–98% dosages, ~8.5 s per prescription.

beforeAfter.before: A pharmacist deciphers the handwriting and re-types it.
beforeAfter.after: OCR and medical NLP extract patient, medicine, dose, frequency and duration; the pharmacist reviews and edits.
Every medicine is matched against 253,973+ records and RxNorm codes.

beforeAfter.before: Re-read, guess, or call the doctor.
beforeAfter.after: Flagged automatically by confidence score, with low, high or urgent review priority.
Stored as structured records that can feed pharmacy and health systems.

lessons.title: The language model is the bottleneck
lessons.text: The Gemini correction step took about 4.5 of the ~8.5 seconds. For production we would cache common corrections, try faster model variants and parallelise the NLP step.

lessons.title: Image quality matters as much as the model
lessons.text: Accuracy drops quickly with blurry or skewed photos. Capture guidance in the upload screen is as important as the OCR engines behind it.

lessons.title: Three OCR vendors means three bills
lessons.text: Running Google, Azure and AWS on every section improves accuracy, but cost per prescription has to be designed in from the start.

lessons.title: A prototype is not a clinical system
lessons.text: Before real patient data, the system needs authentication, audit logs, encryption at rest, HIPAA/GDPR compliance work and clinical validation with pharmacists.

lessons.title: Headless components save weeks
lessons.text: Radix UI primitives gave us keyboard navigation, focus management and screen-reader support without giving up a custom design.

lessons.title: Design tokens first
lessons.text: Setting up colours, spacing and shadows as CSS variables before building screens kept eight pages consistent and made light and dark themes almost free.

lessons.title: Define a workflow once
lessons.text: A single status configuration for orders (label, icon, colour) meant every screen showed order state the same way.

lessons.title: [VERIFY] What's next
lessons.text: [VERIFY] The prototype is front-end only. The next step is a backend with authentication, live order updates over WebSockets and a kitchen display.
